summary: Sprawling across nearly 17 square miles yet home to only about 10,000 people, San Diego Country Estates sits in the inland foothills northeast of Ramona, where the terrain rolls into rocky, chaparral-covered hills and the density — just 604 residents per square mile — is closer to ranchland than suburb. This is definitively a bedroom community: the local economy offers almost no major employers, and the commute to job centers in Escondido, Poway, or central San Diego can easily run 45 minutes to over an hour on winding two-lane roads before reaching any freeway. A median home value of $715,000 against a median household income of roughly $135,000 yields a price-to-income ratio around 5.3 — stretched but not extreme by San Diego County standards — though the near-absence of rental inventory (median rent $2,499) limits flexibility. The payoff is genuine open space: equestrian trails thread through the hills, and average highs hover near 74°F with almost 10 hours of daily sunshine, though summer inland heat pushes well above that. Retail and dining are minimal on-site, with most errands requiring a drive into Ramona or farther. The 1.7% poverty rate and the landscape tell a consistent story: this is a place structured entirely around private acreage and long commutes, and whether that equation works depends almost entirely on how much you value space versus proximity.
